access.title: Roles
access.description: Sets of permissions. A person is given a role on their record, together with where it applies.
access.new_description: A custom role: choose the permissions and whose records they reach.
access.new_copy_description: A copy of an existing role: your changes are saved as a new custom role.
access.list_footer: Predefined roles come with the application and are not edited. Copy gives a custom role to adjust.

notes.predefined: A predefined role comes with the application and is not edited. Copy gives a custom role to adjust.
notes.computed: Its permissions are granted automatically: when the application gets a new permission, the role has it at once. Permissions marked System are held only by the roles that run the system.

access.completed: The role lacked some permissions that its other permissions need, so they are switched on: {names}. Save the role to apply the change.
access.unowned: Includes records nobody owns yet, so the person can pick them up.

qualifier_hint.own: Only records assigned to the person or created by them
qualifier_hint.own_location: Records of the location where the person holds the role
qualifier_hint.all: Every record where the person holds the role

compare.title: Comparison with a predefined role
compare.footer: Shows how far the custom role has moved from the predefined one.

replace.title: Replace the role
replace.footer: Everyone who has this role gets the chosen predefined role at the same place. The same rules apply as when giving a role: you cannot give more than you hold.
replace.moves: People who move to the predefined role: {count}.
replace.done: People moved to the predefined role: {count}

delete.title: Delete the role?
delete.body: The role “{name}” will be deleted. While anyone holds it, it cannot be deleted: replace it first.
delete.failed: The role could not be deleted.

access.roles_footer: A role says what the person may do and whose records they see (their own or all); the place says where. Several roles add up. You can only give what you hold yourself, up to your own place.
access.no_roles_description: Without a role there is nothing to see or do. Add a role and where it applies.
access.remove_body: {name} will no longer have the role “{role}” ({scope}).
access.remove_failed: The role was not removed. Try again.

add.scopes_failed: The places where you can give a role did not load.
add.no_places: You cannot give this person a role anywhere.
add.roles_failed: The roles did not load. Try again.
add.no_roles: You cannot give any role there.
add.role_gives_footer: The role decides; it changes in Roles, not here.

effective.title: What {name} can do
effective.footer: The sum of all the person's roles; it changes by adding or removing roles. Own – records assigned to the person or created by them · Location's – records of their location · All – every record within the role's place.
effective.empty: Without roles there are no permissions.

users.title: Users
users.description: People who sign in: their details, sign-ins and sessions.

create.title: New user
create.subtitle: The person's page opens after saving.

intro.general: Who the person is. Sign-in and sessions have their own pages.
intro.signin: How the person signs in: the lock after wrong passwords, a new password and signing in as them.
intro.sessions: The devices the person is signed in on now.
intro.signins: Every sign-in to the person's account, successful or refused.
intro.changes: What was changed on the person's account and who did it.
intro.activity: What the person did: the records they made, changed or deleted, by area and day.

groups.person_footer: The username is what the person signs in with.

deactivate.title: Deactivate the person
deactivate.row_sub: Signs the person out on every device
deactivate.signs_out_sub: At once, without waiting for the session to end
deactivate.cannot_sign_in_sub: Roles and history stay; activating again restores everything

activate.title: Activate the person?
activate.body: {name} will be able to sign in again. Roles and history stay as they were.
activate.row_sub: Lets the person sign in again; roles and history stay
activate.failed: The person was not activated. Try again.

password.title: New password
password.footer: Nobody can read a password, not even an administrator; only a new one can be set. A new password signs the person out on every device and lifts their lock.

signin.lock_footer: After repeated wrong passwords sign-in is locked for a while. Whoever unlocks it is recorded in Changes and in the sign-in history.
signin.not_locked_sub: It locks after repeated wrong passwords.
signin.unlock_failed: Sign-in was not unlocked. Try again.
signin.password_footer: Nobody can read a password, not even an administrator; only a new one can be set. A new password signs the person out on every device and lifts their lock.
signin.set_password_sub: Tell it to the person in person; they can change it in My profile
signin.as_sub: You see the application as they do, with their access.
signin.as_footer: It is recorded in the sign-in history with your name.

sessions.footer: Signing out takes effect at once: the next click on that device leads to the sign-in. Deactivating and a new password sign the person out everywhere.
sessions.own_footer: This is your account: you sign out your own devices in My profile.
sessions.end_all_body: {name} will have to sign in again on every device, including the sessions somebody opened by signing in as them.

activity.footer: Only what the application records is here. A row done while somebody was signed in as the person says so.
activity.signed_in_as_other: Signed in as, by somebody else

sessions.opened_by_other: Signed in as, by somebody else

signins.footer_user: Every sign-in attempt to the account is recorded, refused ones too.
